31 A student sets up an experiment to investigate double-slit interference.
The student uses light of a single wavelength from a laser to illuminate a double slit so that a
pattern of interference fringes is observed on the screen.
laser
p
screen
fringes
observed here
r
q
double slit
The student finds that the fringes are very close together.
What could the student decrease in order to increase the separation of the fringes on the
screen?
A
the distance p from the laser to the double slit
B
the distance q from the double slit to the screen
C
the separation r of the slits
D
the wavelength of the light from the laser

hints: Notice the labels in the diagram: $q$ is slit-to-screen distance and $r$ is slit separation, while $p$ is only laser-to-slit distance.
Recall the double-slit fringe spacing relation $x = \lambda D / a$, where $D$ is $q$ and $a$ is $r$ in this set-up.
Check which change makes $x$ larger when you must make something smaller: test $q$ on top of the fraction against $r$ on the bottom.
walkthrough: Identify the quantities: slit-to-screen distance $D = q$, slit separation $a = r$, laser wavelength $\lambda$, and fringe separation $x$.
State the governing rule for double-slit interference: $x = \lambda D / a$, which here is $x = \lambda q / r$.
Distance $p$ does not appear in the formula, so changing $p$ does not alter fringe spacing.
Since $x$ is proportional to $q$ and to $\lambda$, decreasing either $q$ or $\lambda$ would decrease $x$, the opposite of what is wanted.
Since $x$ is inversely proportional to $r$, decreasing $r$ increases $x = \lambda q / r$. This is option C.

A.explanation: Distance $p$ controls illumination of the slits, not fringe spacing, so changing $p$ does not change $x$ in $x = \lambda q / r$.

B.explanation: Fringe separation is proportional to $q$, so decreasing $q$ would make the fringes even closer together.

C.explanation: Fringe separation $x = \lambda q / r$ is inversely proportional to slit separation $r$, so decreasing $r$ increases $x$.

D.explanation: Fringe separation is proportional to wavelength $\lambda$, so decreasing $\lambda$ would decrease the fringe separation.
